destination.name: Canberra
destination.tagline: Australia's capital, with free national museums, a lake at its centre and bush hills.
destination.description: Canberra is Australia's planned capital, laid out around Lake Burley Griffin by Walter Burley Griffin. Parliament House, the High Court and the national museums, galleries, library and archives stand in a short run along the lake and Anzac Parade, and most are free to enter. Bush-covered hills such as Mount Ainslie, Black Mountain and Red Hill rise within the city, and Tidbinbilla Nature Reserve and the Murrumbidgee River are a short drive south and west.
whyVisit: See the city from Mount Ainslie

goodToKnow.title: Distances are long
goodToKnow.detail: Institutions sit in a few clusters, so a day on foot or by bike works around the lake. A car or rideshare helps for the outer reserves.

goodToKnow.title: Security screening
goodToKnow.detail: Parliament House and the High Court screen visitors on entry. Allow 15 minutes and leave large bags behind: the High Court bans any over 30 cm.

goodToKnow.title: Check opening days
goodToKnow.detail: The Royal Australian Mint opens shorter hours at weekends, and Blundells Cottage opens only Wednesdays, Saturdays and Sundays.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: Spring and autumn, {months}, bring mild days. Winter nights are frosty.
